**Finding: compliant — no redline proposed.**

The agreement contains no audit, inspection, or verification right binding Mortgage Logic.com. Key checks:

- **§ 5 / § 6 (Compensation; Documentation and Disputes)** — the natural home for a fee/usage audit — runs the other way: TrueLink must supply documentation supporting its charges, and we may contest them.
- **§ 8 (Client covenants)** has no inspection right. "Limitation on Access" (p0053) is our own covenant to restrict Interface access, and the "reasonable access" in p0060 is confined to TrueLink performing Y2K repairs at its own expense.
- **§ 2(e) (p0037)** is the only usage-data provision and it grants *us* real-time access to usage statistics and log files. As host, TrueLink already holds usage data directly, so no audit mechanic is needed.

This sits better than the preferred position (no audit right at all), so there is no frequency, notice, cost-allocation, or system-access exposure to constrain. Importantly, drafting in the preferred limits would require first *creating* a Vendor audit right against us — a net loss — so the correct action is to leave the silence intact and resist any Vendor attempt to add one on redline exchange.
